subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should plugin-runtime `sessions.patch` fail closed for every legacy ownerless session row, even when that stops an existing plugin workflow after upgrade?
rationale: The code can enforce either boundary safely, but repository history does not establish whether ownerless persisted rows must be denied immediately or migrated before enforcement.

options.title: Fail Closed
options.body: Reject plugin-runtime patches to ownerless rows and document and prove the upgrade behavior before merge.

options.title: Migrate Ownership
options.body: Add an explicit doctor or ownership migration that establishes safe ownership before enforcing the restriction.

options.title: Temporary Compatibility
options.body: Preserve narrowly defined ownerless-row access until migration is available, accepting a weaker isolation boundary.

recommendation.title: Fail Closed
recommendation.body: Reject plugin-runtime patches to ownerless rows and document and prove the upgrade behavior before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged history shows the strongest ownership signal across both the affected Gateway handler and shared session-store surfaces.
